title: C15 Test 2 Passage 1 阅读复盘
subtitle: Could urban engineers learn from dance?  解题方法与习惯复盘

sources.label: C15 Test2 Passage 1.pdf（原文及实际高亮）
sources.text:
A
The way we travel around cities has a major impact on whether they are sustainable. Transportation is estimated to account for 30% of energy consumption in most of the world's most developed nations, so lowering the need for energy-using vehicles is essential for decreasing the environmental impact of mobility. But as more and more people move to cities, it is important to think about other kinds of sustainable travel too. The ways we travel affect our physical and mental health, our social lives, our access to work and culture, and the air we breathe. Engineers are tasked with changing how we travel round cities through urban design, but the engineering industry still works on the assumptions that led to the creation of the energy-consuming transport systems we have now: the emphasis placed solely on efficiency, speed, and quantitative data. We need radical changes, to make it healthier, more enjoyable, and less environmentally damaging to travel around cities.

B
Dance might hold some of the answers. That is not to suggest everyone should dance their way to work, however healthy and happy it might make us, but rather that the techniques used by choreographers to experiment with and design movement in dance could provide engineers with tools to stimulate new ideas in city-making. Richard Sennett, an influential urbanist and sociologist who has transformed ideas about the way cities are made, argues that urban design has suffered from a separation between mind and body since the introduction of the architectural blueprint.

C
Whereas medieval builders improvised and adapted construction through their intimate knowledge of materials and personal experience of the conditions on a site, building designs are now conceived and stored in media technologies that detach the designer from the physical and social realities they are creating. While the design practices created by these new technologies are essential for managing the technical complexity of the modern city, they have the drawback of simplifying reality in the process.

D
To illustrate, Sennett discusses the Peachtree Center in Atlanta, USA, a development typical of the modernist approach to urban planning prevalent in the 1970s. Peachtree created a grid of streets and towers intended as a new pedestrian-friendly downtown for Atlanta. According to Sennett, this failed because its designers had invested too much faith in computer-aided design to tell them how it would operate. They failed to take into account that purpose-built street cafés could not operate in the hot sun without the protective awnings common in older buildings, and would need energy-consuming air conditioning instead, or that its giant car park would feel so unwelcoming that it would put people off getting out of their cars. What seems entirely predictable and controllable on screen has unexpected results when translated into reality.

E
The same is true in transport engineering, which uses models to predict and shape the way people move through the city. Again, these models are necessary, but they are built on specific world views in which certain forms of efficiency and safety are considered and other experiences of the city ignored. Designs that seem logical in models appear counter-intuitive in the actual experience of their users. The guard rails that will be familiar to anyone who has attempted to cross a British road, for example, were an engineering solution to pedestrian safety based on models that prioritise the smooth flow of traffic. On wide major roads, they often guide pedestrians to specific crossing points and slow down their progress across the road by using staggered access points to divide the crossing into two – one for each carriageway. In doing so they make crossings feel longer, introducing psychological barriers greatly impacting those that are the least mobile, and encouraging others to make dangerous crossings to get around the guard rails. These barriers don't just make it harder to cross the road: they divide communities and decrease opportunities for healthy transport. As a result, many are now being removed, causing disruption, cost, and waste.

F
If their designers had had the tools to think with their bodies – like dancers – and imagine how these barriers would feel, there might have been a better solution. In order to bring about fundamental changes to the ways we use our cities, engineering will need to develop a richer understanding of why people move in certain ways, and how this movement affects them. Choreography may not seem an obvious choice for tackling this problem. Yet it shares with engineering the aim of designing patterns of movement within limitations of space. It is an art form developed almost entirely by trying out ideas with the body, and gaining instant feedback on how the results feel. Choreographers have deep understanding of the psychological, aesthetic, and physical implications of different ways of moving.

G
Observing the choreographer Wayne McGregor, cognitive scientist David Kirsh described how he 'thinks with the body'. Kirsh argues that by using the body to simulate outcomes, McGregor is able to imagine solutions that would not be possible using purely abstract thought. This kind of physical knowledge is valued in many areas of expertise, but currently has no place in formal engineering design processes. A suggested method for transport engineers is to improvise design solutions and get instant feedback about how they would work from their own experience of them, or model designs at full scale in the way choreographers experiment with groups of dancers. Above all, perhaps, they might learn to design for emotional as well as functional effects.

sources.text: 用户说明：绿色为正确答案，红色为错答。1 B；2 D→C；3 F；4 A→D；5 C→E；6 E→A；7 safety；8 traffic；9 carriageway；10 mobile；11 dangerous；12 communities；13 healthy。摘要填空要求 ONE WORD ONLY。

overview.focus: 先练两件事：读题时保留“对象＋关系＋限制”；找到充分证据就作答，卡住则留下缺项再回查。第 2、4、5、6 题的错误候选都未满足完整要求；这不等于已确认你当时漏读了条件。

type_comments.段落信息匹配: 错在第 2、4、5、6 题；重点核对完整要求，并区分相似段落。
type_comments.摘要填空: 7 题均正确，答案集中在 E 段；结果不能单独证明当时找得快。

passage_map.use: 出行方式影响人的生活 → 第 6 题。别把首句城市可持续性当作同一对象。
不主张跳舞上班，而是借鉴编舞 → 第 1 题。留意否定与真正建议的边界。
现场经验与媒介技术设计 → 第 2 题。比较的是方法，不是新旧建筑名称。
烈日下咖啡馆运营受阻 → 第 4 题。查气候、忽略和意外问题的因果链。
第 7—13 题集中于第 4—7 句；拆除原因对应第 5 题，可复用同段位置。

passage_map.role: 编舞与工程的共同目标
passage_map.use: 空间限制下设计运动模式 → 第 3 题。it 回指 choreography。

passage_map.role: 身体试验怎样用于设计
passage_map.use: 补全全文论证：身体模拟、即时反馈、情感与功能。本题组无直接答案。

questions.title: 过去与现在的建造方法

requirement.text: an example of a contrast between past and present approaches to building
requirement.meaning: 对比的两端是过去与现在；比较的对象是建造／设计方法，不能只有新旧事物。

evidence.quote: Whereas medieval builders improvised and adapted construction through their intimate knowledge of materials and personal experience of the conditions on a site, building designs are now conceived and stored in media technologies
evidence.explanation: Whereas 对比古今：过去凭材料知识和现场经验调整施工；现在借媒介技术构思、保存设计。

questions.comparison: D 的 modernist approach／older buildings 涉及项目与旧建筑遮篷；C 则对比两种建造方法：现场经验调整与媒介技术设计。比较对象不同。

cause.observation: 题干未标 past and present；C 只标现在做法，未标过去一端。标记提示查全条件，不能证明当时漏读。
cause.self_check: 当时只查“有对比”，查 04；读懂 C 的两种方法仍选 D，查 05。记不清则待确认。
cause.stage: 读题保留条件 → 比较候选

questions.action: 读 contrast 时先确定“古今＋建造方法”。扫到 Whereas，分别说出过去凭现场经验、现在借媒介设计；两端及维度齐全就选 C。若仍留 D，只回查 D 是否也给出这两种方法。

questions.title: 忽略气候造成的意外问题

requirement.text: reference to an unforeseen problem arising from ignoring the climate
requirement.meaning: 必须同时有“忽略当地气候”和“因此发生意外问题”，并形成因果关系。

evidence.quote: They failed to take into account that purpose-built street cafés could not operate in the hot sun without the protective awnings common in older buildings
evidence.explanation: failed to take into account 对应 ignoring；hot sun 对应 climate。忽略烈日下的遮阳需求，导致咖啡馆无法运营。
emphasis: could not operate in the hot sun

evidence.quote: What seems entirely predictable and controllable on screen has unexpected results when translated into reality.
evidence.explanation: unexpected results 对应 unforeseen problem，确认这是意外问题。

questions.comparison: A 讲交通能耗对环境的影响；D 讲气候条件被忽略后，具体设施出现运营问题。前者是“交通影响环境”，后者是“忽略气候导致问题”，因果方向不同。

cause.observation: 题干只标 unforeseen problem；D 标了意外结果的总结，未标烈日与遮篷的原因句。A 的环境议题并不满足题目因果。
cause.self_check: 当时误解 climate，查 01；懂词却只找 problem，查 04。现在能解释不证明当时会。
cause.stage: 理解 climate → 核对因果

questions.action: 把目标记为“忽略气候→意外问题”。扫到 hot sun，读全 failed to take into account 到 could not operate，再用段尾 unexpected results 确认意外性；条件齐全即选，不继续展开停车场。

questions.title: 帮助行人的措施为何被撤回

requirement.text: why some measures intended to help people are being reversed
requirement.meaning: 找出原本想帮助人的措施、撤回／拆除动作，以及为什么这样做。

evidence.quote: were an engineering solution to pedestrian safety
evidence.explanation: 主语是 guard rails；原来设置护栏是为了解决行人安全问题。

evidence.quote: they divide communities and decrease opportunities for healthy transport. As a result, many are now being removed, causing disruption, cost, and waste.
evidence.explanation: As a result 前是拆除原因；being removed 是撤回动作；causing…是拆除后果。

questions.comparison: C 只说技术简化现实的 drawback，没有措施被撤回的动作。E 的 being removed 对应 reversed。disruption、cost、waste 是拆除带来的后果，不是拆除的理由；理由在 As a result 之前。

cause.observation: 题干已标 reversed；E 标了安全目的与部分副作用，未标拆除动作。填空全对不能证明当时复用了该段。
cause.self_check: 当时未认出 removed 对应 reversed，查 02；懂撤回却凭 drawback 定案，查 04。
cause.stage: 识别撤回改写 → 回查原因

questions.action: 把目标记为“帮助措施为何撤回”。做完摘要后顺读 being removed，回看 As a result 前的副作用，并用 pedestrian safety 核对原目的；三项齐全即选。不要把拆除后的 cost 当作原因。

questions.title: 交通出行如何影响人的生活

requirement.text: reference to how transport has an impact on human lives
requirement.meaning: 核对“交通／出行方式”如何影响人的生活；不能只凭同样涉及人或健康就定段。

evidence.quote: The ways we travel affect our physical and mental health, our social lives, our access to work and culture, and the air we breathe.
evidence.explanation: The ways we travel 对应 transport，affect 对应 has an impact on。后面列出身心健康、社交、工作文化机会及呼吸空气，落实 human lives。

questions.comparison: E 也写心理障碍、社区和健康出行，确实相关；但主线是“护栏→过街障碍与出行机会”。A 明确给出“出行方式→人的多方面生活”。不能仅因 E 是具体例子就排除，要比较影响的主体与对象。

cause.observation: A 的首句 impact 已标，生活影响句未标；E 的生活话题已标。不能据此断定当时读过 A 的证据。
cause.self_check: 当时找到 A 第 4 句仍选 E，查 05；没找到该句，查 03。记不清则待确认。
cause.stage: 定位生活影响 → 对齐主体与对象

questions.action: 把目标记为“出行方式→人的生活”。扫到 travel／affect 后对齐影响者与受影响者，用健康、社交等具体表现确认；若 A/E 犹豫，只比较两段这条关系，不重译整段。

causes.training: 对比题查两端与对象；原因题查原因与结果；撤回题查措施、动作与理由。缺一项先不定案。
并排写两个候选的“主体→动作／影响→对象”，圈出不符合题干的部分。
检查 climate 与 environmental impact 的区别，再判断是词义问题还是条件遗漏。
核对 reversed ↔ being removed 的对应；会解释后，在新题中检验能否自行认出。
从题干 transport／human lives 找 travel、affect 和生活领域；找到后再核对范围。

method.reading: 匹配题先看完整组目标；填空题先看 ONE WORD ONLY，并把每空改述成一个问题。题旁只需极短提示。
method.locating: 摘要标题找 E；匹配题一次扫段服务多题。全文地图用于复盘，不要求考场先给 A—G 写摘要。
method.deciding: 从扫读切到局部细读。核对对象、关系和本题限制；填空再检查字数、拼写与原文词形。
method.checking: 本轮只练上面两个动作。比较难度相近的新题组；同时看错误类型、正确率与总用时，不只看速度。
method.keeping: 7—13 全对，保留现有正确结果；具体用了什么方法仍待确认。F 的共同目标标记可继续作为回查依据。

speed_plan.context: 可尝试以下路线。C15 未记录用时；个人速度背景是 C14 Test 3 整套约 75 分钟、最终换算 8 分，60 分钟成绩未知。目标是在新题中减少无效回读，同时守住准确率。

steps.action: 先读 1—6 的完整目标：未提议／古今方法／共同目标／气候因果／撤回原因／生活影响。再用摘要题面 Guard rails 扫描原文。
steps.saves: 匹配题共享待找目标；摘要用辨识度高的入口缩小范围。

steps.action: 定位护栏段后，核对每空两侧条件，按 E 第 4—7 句实际顺序做 7—13；7/8、10/11、12/13 共用句子。顺读第 8 句处理第 5 题。
steps.saves: 一次定位覆盖 8 题；省去每题单独全文检索。

steps.action: 带着其余五题的目标，按段扫读并更新未完成题。遇否定、对比、共同目标、气候因果或生活影响，再局部细读；不为每题重启全文。
steps.saves: 让一次段落扫读服务多题；只精读候选证据。

speed_plan.stop_rule: 条件齐全就作答并离开。一轮针对性检查仍无新发现，保留“候选位置＋缺哪项”再转题，题组末先回收已有候选的题。暂放依据是没有进展，不是每题统一计秒。
speed_plan.practice: 旧题只练动作，不作为提速证据。下一套新题到 60 分钟保留答案，核对限时完成数与正确数；补做另记用时和成绩。只对卡题补记主要环节，不逐题计秒。

habits.name: 先明确完整目标，再找位置
habits.action: 脑中保留“对象＋关系＋限制”。第 5 题不能只记 reversed，还要保留 why；第 8 题要问哪种流动不能受阻。
habits.pass_check: 对新题核对时，能指出每个必要条件的依据；做完后检查有没有“找对话题却漏关系”的错题。
habits.record: 题组结束记：漏掉必要条件的题号；没有就记 0。题干标记少不等于动作完成。

habits.name: 证据齐全就离开，卡住只查缺项
habits.trigger: 已有候选答案，或开始反复读同一处时。
habits.action: 先给一句证据理由；充分就填。仍不确定，留下候选位置和缺项，转题后再定向回查。例：第 2 题只比较 C/D 的建造方法。
habits.pass_check: 回查有明确缺项；修改已确认答案有新证据。仅因不放心重读时，能及时发现并停止。
habits.record: 每组记无新证据的反复回查题号、总用时与正确数／题数；不靠漏查条件换速度。

add.observed: 已标现在的设计方法；未标过去一端。
add.quote: Whereas medieval builders improvised and adapted construction
add.reason: 补过去一端，与已标 now 对读。

add.observed: 已标段末意外结果；未标烈日与遮篷。
add.quote: street cafés could not operate in the hot sun without the protective awnings
add.reason: 补具体问题；回读同句 failed to take into account 确认原因。

add.observed: 已标安全目的、心理障碍和危险穿行；未标拆除。
add.quote: As a result, many are now being removed
add.reason: 保存撤回动作；理由回看前文。

add.observed: 首句 impact 已标；生活影响句未标。
add.quote: The ways we travel affect our physical and mental health, our social lives
add.reason: 标出出行对人的影响；回读同句余下生活领域。

reduce.reason: 过于通用；需回查时以 travel 或具体影响对象定位。

reduce.observed: What seems entirely predictable and controllable on screen has unexpected results when translated into reality.
reduce.reason: 保留结果路标；具体原因由上方烈日句保存。

keep.observed: Yet it shares with engineering the aim of designing patterns of movement within limitations of space
keep.reason: 共同主体、目标和空间限制都在，值得保留。

highlights.question_adjustments: 第 2 题补 past and present；第 4 题补 ignoring the climate；第 5 题保留 reversed 并补 why；第 6 题补 transport 与 human lives。
highlights.boundary: 以上对照两份 PDF 的实际标记。未标不等于没读过；临时路标可保留，不要求把所有答案句涂满。

answer_routes.path: 扫 dance 附近的否定建议，找到 not to suggest 后读完整转折。
answer_routes.check: 跳舞上班有 healthy and happy 的吸引力，但作者明确不主张；不是后半句真正提议的编舞方法。
answer_routes.time_saver: 读完否定与转折边界即可；不展开后面的 Sennett 人物介绍。
answer_routes.test_point: 否定范围与让步：有吸引力，但不被提议

answer_routes.path: 扫建造话题中的成对时间词；识别 Whereas、medieval builders—now。
answer_routes.check: 过去凭现场经验调整施工，现在借媒介技术设计；两端都在比较建造／设计方法。
answer_routes.time_saver: 同一句查完两端方法即停；不再为了 modern／old 遍搜别段。
answer_routes.test_point: 比较双方和维度：古今＋建造方法

answer_routes.path: 扫两者的共同点；shares…aim 对应共同目标，回读 it 指谁。
answer_routes.check: it 指 choreography；共同目标是受空间限制地设计运动模式。
answer_routes.time_saver: 只补读 it 的指向；共同目标齐全后，不展开后文编舞训练。
answer_routes.test_point: 共同目标与指代：两者共享什么

answer_routes.path: 扫具体气候条件，遇 hot sun 前查遗漏，后查运营问题。
answer_routes.check: failed to take into account＋烈日下缺遮篷＋咖啡馆无法运营；unexpected results 确认意外。
answer_routes.time_saver: 精读烈日与遮篷的因果；本题不用展开同句另一个停车场问题。
answer_routes.test_point: 因果方向：忽略气候 → 意外问题

answer_routes.path: 扫撤回动作，找到 being removed 后回读；可复用护栏摘要的段落。
answer_routes.location: E 第 8 句，回查第 4、6—7 句
answer_routes.check: 原为安全，后有危险穿行和社区分割，因此拆除。disruption/cost/waste 是拆除后果。
answer_routes.time_saver: 复用 7—13 题已找到的护栏段；顺读拆除句，省去全文重搜。
answer_routes.test_point: 目的、撤回原因与撤回后果分开

answer_routes.path: 扫 travel 与健康、社交等生活领域；识别 affect 的影响关系。
answer_routes.check: 出行方式影响身心健康、社交、工作文化与空气；首句 impact 影响的是城市可持续性。
answer_routes.time_saver: 比较“谁影响谁”后定案；不因 E 的局部近义词反复改选。
answer_routes.test_point: 影响关系：谁影响谁，不能只对上话题

answer_routes.path: 用护栏标题找到整组出处，再查设置目的：solution to pedestrian…。
answer_routes.check: safety：of pedestrians 对应 pedestrian safety；原文取词，每空只填一个词。
answer_routes.time_saver: 本句连做 7、8 两空；一次定位两题，不每空重新找护栏。
answer_routes.test_point: 所属与目的：改善行人的哪一方面

answer_routes.path: 接第 7 题同句，找 not disrupted 的改写 smooth flow。
answer_routes.check: traffic：not disrupted 对应 smooth flow；核对流动的是车流，不能只凭名词词性取词。
answer_routes.time_saver: 接第 7 题同句后半取词；核对 flow 的对象后移到下一句。
answer_routes.test_point: 动作对象：哪种流动要保持顺畅

answer_routes.path: 往下一句找 access points，再读 divide…into two 与 one for each。
answer_routes.check: carriageway：divide…into two—one for each 对应 one…at a time；保留单数。
answer_routes.time_saver: 接上题读下一句，查 one for each；不从段首重新读。
answer_routes.test_point: 数量与单位：一次过一侧什么

answer_routes.path: 顺读 difficulties 的改写 barriers，随后找受影响更大的人群。
answer_routes.check: mobile：the least mobile 指行动最不便的人群，对应题干 less…people 的概括；取形容词。
answer_routes.time_saver: 本句一并处理 10、11；先查受影响人群，再查另一后果。
answer_routes.test_point: 人群限定：受影响更大的是哪类人

answer_routes.path: 接同句 and，查 others 的过街行为；识别 crossings 的修饰词。
answer_routes.check: dangerous：make dangerous crossings 改写为 cross…in a dangerous way，行为与修饰同时对应。
answer_routes.time_saver: 接第 10 题同句的 and；只核过街行为，不重读设置护栏的目的。
answer_routes.test_point: 词性与句式改写：危险穿行 → 怎样穿行

answer_routes.path: 读下一句，these barriers 指护栏；separate 对应 divide。
answer_routes.check: communities：separate 对应 divide；核对宾语，原样保留复数 communities。
answer_routes.time_saver: 本句连做 12、13；先取 divide 的宾语，再看后半交通方式。
answer_routes.test_point: 动词宾语与复数：护栏分隔什么

answer_routes.entry: transport that are…；more difficult to introduce
answer_routes.path: 接同句 and，识别 decrease opportunities，再找 transport 的修饰词。
answer_routes.check: healthy：healthy transport 变成 transport that are healthy；decrease opportunities 对应更难推广。
answer_routes.time_saver: 接第 12 题同句取修饰词；本空不必扩读下一句拆除后果。
answer_routes.test_point: 修饰关系：哪种交通方式
